title: Wake-up stroke - unknown last known well
objectives: BGL before calling it a stroke (mimic r/o)
TLKW = last time at baseline, not time found; probe overnight + phone contacts
Stroke screen + FAST-ED; Stroke Alert <10 min of recognition
Thrombolytic checklist incl. anticoagulant last dose
Direct to UVMMC, scene <15 min, witness rides or phone # obtained
resources: Glucometer, monitor/12-lead, O2, suction, IV kit + NS 250 mL, stretcher (HOB 30 deg). Scene ~12 min from UVMMC (comprehensive stroke / thrombectomy center).
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 37 Lakeshore Dr, Colchester, for a 71-year-old male, possible stroke. Caller is his wife; he can't speak. Patient is breathing. Time out 0707.

scene.location: Kitchen of a split-level home, 4 steps to front door. ~12 min from UVMMC.
scene.setup: Pt slumped in kitchen chair, coffee mug tipped over, cold coffee on table. Wife's cell phone on counter. Pill bottles by sink.
scene.moulage: None needed beyond tags; actor plays R-sided weakness.
scene.roles: Pt actor (aphasic); wife (history, "he was fine at bedtime"); evaluator plays daughter by phone + UVMMC.

patient.name: Richard Desautels
patient.cc: Can't talk, R arm limp - found by wife 0655
patient.on_arrival: Seated, slumped to R, eyes open, R arm hanging limp. Says "no, no" to every question. Follows "squeeze my hand" with L only.

SAMPLE: Can't speak, R arm/leg weak, R face droop
**Apixaban 5 mg BID - stopped ~2 wk ago** (nosebleeds), metoprolol 50 mg, lisinopril 20 mg
**A-fib**, HTN. No prior stroke, no seizures, no recent surgery/head trauma
Bed 2215 normal. Wife woke 0655, found him at table like this
OPQRST: Unknown - **found** 0655. Daughter spoke w/ him 0550 (only if probed)

primary: Patent; pooling saliva R mouth corner
GCS 13 (E4 V3 M6). **R face droop, R arm flaccid, aphasic**. BGL needed
No head trauma, no tongue bite, no incontinence
**HIGH**: acute stroke, probable LVO. TLKW not yet known
secondary: **Gaze deviated L**, won't cross midline to R
Only "no, no"; can't name objects or repeat
R leg weak, can't lift off floor
Drools R; coughs on sip (do not test w/ fluid)

vitals.other: Irregularly irregular. Gaze L. R face/arm/leg weak, aphasic
Vomits, gurgling, coughing. E3 V2 M6

vitals.trigger: ~2 min after suction, L lateral/upright, O2 NC
vitals.other: Airway clear. Lungs clear. Report GCS drop to UVMMC

flow.give: Read dispatch. Wife: "I just found him like this, he can't talk!" Stage **A** as obtained.
Wife: "He was fine at bedtime, 10:15. Is it too late for the clot-buster?" Give TLKW clues only when asked.

branches.if: Crew uses time found (0655) as onset
Crew asks if he got up overnight / who saw him
branches.then: wife: "Heard him up at 5:30, always is." Daughter calls wife's phone: "Talked to Dad at 5:50, he was fine." TLKW 0550
still alert criteria (FAST-ED >= 4, <24 h); tPA window missed - debrief

flow.give: Wife: "Can we wait for our daughter? She's 10 minutes out."

branches.if: Crew waits for daughter or intercept
branches.then: scene >15 min; critical (evaluator discretion). Wife rides instead

expected: Stroke Alert to UVMMC <10 min of recognition
Thrombolytic checklist; apixaban last dose ~2 wk
Direct to UVMMC, no wait for intercept

flow.give: Stage **B**. Wife offers his morning pills and water.

branches.if: Pills, water or ASA given by mouth

branches.then: no AEMT treatment; report BP, let UVMMC manage
Stage **C**; expect suction, L lateral/upright, O2 to 94-98% -> Stage **D**; GCS drop reported (hemorrhage?)

flow.give: Stage **E**. Evaluator plays UVMMC stroke team at the door.
expected: Report: TLKW + source, FAST-ED, BGL, anticoag
SIREN: TLKW, alert time, scene times

critical: No BGL before stroke alert / mimic not considered (2.26A)
TLKW reported as time found, or not established (2.26A)
No stroke screen or severity score (FAST-ED)
No Stroke Alert, or >10 min after recognition (2.26A)
Not direct to UVMMC; scene delayed for intercept or family
No witness on board and no witness phone number
differentials: A-fib off apixaban, aphasia, R hemiparesis, gaze L, FAST-ED 6
No headache reported; can't exclude in field
No seizure hx, no tongue bite/incontinence
debrief: How did you get from 2215 to 0550? Why does it matter?
What does TLKW mean when someone wakes up with symptoms?
Which FAST-ED findings scored, and what does >= 4 suggest?
Why is the anticoagulant last dose part of the alert?
Why HOB 30 and NPO? What would you do differently on vomiting?

crew_card.dispatch: 37 Lakeshore Dr, Colchester. 71 y/o M, possible stroke. Can't speak. Breathing. Caller: wife.
crew_card.on_arrival: Kitchen. Older man slumped in chair, coffee spilled, right arm hanging. Wife beside him, upset.

actor_card.Act: Eyes open, slumped to R. R arm limp, R leg weak. Drool from R mouth corner. Look to your L.
actor_card.Speech: Only "no, no" to every question. Get frustrated. Can't name a pen or repeat a phrase.
actor_card.Commands: Squeeze/raise L hand when asked. R arm drops when lifted.
actor_card.If given water: Cough, choke, spill it out R side.
actor_card.If vomit inject: Gag, cough, groggier; open eyes only to voice.
actor_card.Wife: Fine at bedtime 2215. ONLY if asked about the night: heard him up at 5:30. Mention he quit his blood thinner only if asked about meds.
actor_card.Daughter (phone): Calls only if crew asks who talked to him: "I talked to Dad at 5:50, he was fine."

show_cards.title: 12-LEAD
show_cards.caption: Computer interpretation: Atrial fibrillation 104. Nonspecific ST-T abnormality. No acute MI criteria.  Simulated tracing - not to scale.
show_cards.cue: Show when acquired; must not delay transport
